notes: Facility is widely rated the best arena in the game, and the data says why: twenty-nine doors across a looping layout, which makes it the map with the most ways to arrive somewhere unexpected.
It is a converted campaign map, so its pickups are the standard conversion loadout rather than hand-placed. Armour is not the contested prize it is on the purpose-built arenas -- the doors are.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: This is a doorway map above all else: nearly every engagement starts at a threshold, and knowing which doors connect is worth more than any weapon.
nuance.because: The arena setup carries twenty-nine Door records, the most of any multiplayer stage except Bunker.

nuance.claim: The corridors loop rather than dead-end, so a player who breaks contact can come back around behind the opponent who chased them.
Because everything loops, holding a corridor means being approached from both ends; positions have to be rotated rather than held.
Pickups here are the normalised conversion set rather than hand-tuned, so armour control matters less than on the purpose-built arenas and map knowledge matters more.
nuance.because: Facility, Archives, Caverns, Egypt and Bunker all carry an identical two Armour, sixteen AmmoBox, nine Collectable loadout, unlike the dedicated arenas which range from one to three armours and eleven to thirty-one ammo boxes.

nuance.claim: The vent system connects rooms without using their doors, which defeats anyone watching or mining a doorway.
Doors are so numerous that mining them is inefficient; the vents are few, heavily used and approached blind, which makes them the better placement.
Several partitions are tinted glass, which conceals more than clear glass while still being destructible, so a wall that hid you a moment ago may not next time.
nuance.because: The arena carries eight TintedGlass records.

nuance.claim: With eight spawn points, holding a reappearance point is wasted effort; controlling the door network is the better use of position.
nuance.because: The arena carries eight Spawn records, joint most of any stage.

nuance.claim: Doors are audible and visible as they open, so approaching through one gives warning; the vents and already-open routes are quieter.
Sightlines are short and broken by doors and corners, so precision long-range weapons are weak here and fast-firing ones are strong.
With one-hit kills, whoever is already aiming at a door when it opens wins, so the mode becomes a contest of predicting which door an opponent will use.
The looping layout is ideal for an unarmed carrier, who can circle indefinitely without ever being cornered as long as they keep moving.
A marked holder should sit where only one door can be entered from, forcing the three hunters to arrive one at a time into a one-shot weapon.
The dense corridor network carries sound from rooms that are not actually adjacent, so audio gives presence but not direction.
The map's pale interior makes light-coloured characters harder to pick out than dark ones, reversing the usual advice.
